entries.what_happened: Five manuscripts, all about fourfolds, each claiming a termination result in dimension four. None treats dimension five or higher. (a) 'Termination of generalized log canonical flips on compact Kähler fourfolds' (October 7, 2026; main theorem thm:main): for a normal irreducible globally Weil Q-factorial compact Kähler fourfold X_0 with effective rational boundary B_0 of coefficients in [0,1], and a rational b-divisor represented by an analytically nef Q-Cartier divisor on a projective model, with (X_0, B_0+M) generalized log canonical, every sequence of flips X_i -> Z_i <- X_{i+1} (projective small maps with connected fibres, Z_i normal compact Kähler, neither map an isomorphism, -D_i f_i-ample, D_{i+1} f_i^+-ample) is finite. M=0 gives the ordinary lc case. (b) 'Termination of generalized-canonical flips on compact Kähler fourfolds' (October 6, 2026; build/build/paper.tex, theorem thm:termination): the same conclusion with boundary coefficients in [0,1) and generalized canonical hypotheses (every log discrepancy on X_0 positive, exceptional ones at least 1). (c) 'Termination for projective log canonical fourfolds with rational boundary' (September 24, 2026): for a projective lc fourfold with rational boundary over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, (i) every negative extremal ray has its contraction and, when birational, a positive model; (ii) every permitted program has finitely many birational steps for every choice of rays, where a permitted program steps by contracting a negative extremal ray of relative Picard number one, followed by a divisorial contraction, a projective small flip, or a mixed step; (iii) maximal programs end at a nef lc model or a Mori fibre space. No Q-factoriality or pseudo-effectivity is assumed. (d) 'Finite ordinary minimal model programs on compact Kähler fourfolds' (October 6, 2026; theorem thm:finite): for a normal globally Weil Q-factorial compact Kähler fourfold with klt effective rational boundary, every maximal program of ordinary negative steps (projective divisorial contractions and flips of D-negative extremal rays) terminates. The endpoint is nef when K+Δ is pseudo-effective, and otherwise a projective Mori fibre space over a base of dimension below four. Its finiteness of flip tails is taken from (a), via its Corollary repair:cor:existing. (e) 'Finite ordinary minimal model programs on compact Kähler fourfolds' (September 24, 2026; an earlier paper with the same title as (d)): for the same klt Kähler setting, there exists one finite ordinary program, obtained by a suitable choice of steps, with the same endpoint classification. It does not claim termination for every choice.
entries.delivers: Dimension four only, in the stated classes. (a) and (b) answer no for the flip sequences they describe: on Kähler, globally Weil Q-factorial fourfolds with a fixed rational nef b-divisor, no infinite sequence of such flips exists. They need no pseudo-effectivity or scaling, and the flips need not be extremal and the Z_i need not share a base. (c) answers no for every permitted program, hence for flips occurring as steps of such programs, on projective lc fourfolds with rational boundary, without Q-factoriality. Its singularity class is wider than (d)'s, but its flips must each contract a relative Picard number one extremal ray. (d) answers no for every maximal ordinary program on klt Kähler fourfolds: an infinite run would contain an infinite tail of flips, which (d) excludes by citing (a). Its divisorial steps are finite by a cycle count. (e) gives only existence of one finite program and says nothing about infinite sequences in general. The manuscripts do not claim to settle the bullet as the list words it. (c) says it proves 'the projective four-dimensional case of the Termination of Flips Conjecture for ordinary log canonical pairs with rational boundary'. (e) says it gives 'an affirmative solution of the finite-program form of the rational klt fourfold minimal model conjecture' in the Kähler category, and does not state that form. Against the bullet's parts: (1) dimensions: only n = 4 is treated; (2) objects: flips of pairs in the classes above, not all flips; (3) existence is not asked, but (a) and (b) state they do not assert existence of contractions or flips, while (c) and (d) construct the steps they use; (4) each 'no' covers only its class.
entries.remains: If the claims hold, still open for this bullet: every dimension n >= 5. In dimension four: flip sequences outside the classes above, including non-Q-factorial ambients for (a), (b), (d) and (e); non-Kähler ambients or non-projective flips for (a) and (b); boundaries with coefficients outside [0,1], non-lc pairs for (c), and non-klt pairs for (d) and (e); varying nef data for (a) and (b); arbitrary flip sequences that are not programs in (c), (d) and (e); flips whose negative contraction has relative Picard number above one, in (c); existence of flips in (a) and (b); termination for every choice of steps in (e). No manuscript treats the footnote's class directly: klt flips, projective over one fixed normal base. None of them fixes a base, and (a), (b), (d) and (e) add Kähler and global Weil Q-factoriality hypotheses.
entries.direction: proves termination of flip sequences in dimension four for the stated classes, answering no there only; (e) proves only existence of one finite program
entries.conditional_on: (a) cites from (d), without proving them: special termination for generalized dlt pairs in dimension four (its Theorem 11.3), relative continuation and finite runs (Propositions 9.7 and 9.9), exact extraction (Proposition 9.11), crepant gdlt modification (Proposition 11.4), and low places (Lemma 4.2(i)). It cites from (b): the common-model construction (Proposition 2.1), analytic negativity (Lemma 2.2) and terminal smoothness in codimension two (Lemma 2.3). Its difficulty and branch steps follow the projective methods of ProjectiveLCFourfolds, the companion (c), at Section 3 Proposition 3.4, Definition 4.2, Lemma 4.3, Section 5 Lemma 5.2, Section 6.1 and Section 7, with analytic steps supplied. (b) relies on Wang's analytic negativity lemma (external), and on (e)'s Lemma 2.3(i), Lemma 4.4 and Section 4.1. (d) relies on (a)'s Theorem 1.1 to exclude infinite flip tails, through its Corollary repair:cor:existing, and on its own relative and special-termination sections. (c) relies only on published inputs listed in its introduction: cone and contraction theorems, BCHM, Birkar's lc flip and complemented-pair existence results, surface mld ACC, dlt special termination, and Hodge theory. Its endpoint consequences (semiampleness, complements, Cartier sections) use three OpenAI companion preprints that are not part of its termination claim. (e) relies on Hacon and Xie (arXiv:2607.24986, July 2026) for the contractions and for finiteness of marked models away from scaling parameter zero, on Birkar (2009) for the limiting-model strategy, and on Matsumura and Zhong.
entries.doubts: (1) (a) and (d) depend on each other: (d) uses (a)'s flip theorem for infinite flip tails, and (a) uses (d)'s special-termination and relative-program results. (d)'s Section 6 opening states that those results do not depend on its finite-program theorem. The loop is between papers, and that assertion is the one a reader must check. (2) (d)'s intrinsic formulation, with a canonical rational line bundle in place of a canonical divisor, is argued in one paragraph that ends 'leaves that proof unchanged'. (3) (b) says it 'reproduces these arguments in full and invokes no termination theorem', yet its negativity, terminal-smoothness and cycle-comparison inputs are cited to (e). (4) The introduction of (a) summarises its branch and difficulty estimates by method (Quot parameters, local factorisation, purity). The statements of the sections that carry them are not verified here. (5) (c)'s field-transfer lemma gives its key degree-constancy step with alternative justifications ('or follows from constancy of its Euler characteristic') and is compressed. (6) (e) claims an 'affirmative solution' of a conjecture whose form the text does not state.
